clues: This port city in the south of India lies just south of Puducherry. It was a key port in the days of British rule.
Most rain here comes with the north east monsoon, not the south west one. That late rain, from October to January, far beats the June rains.
French and British troops clashed here in 1758, in the midst of a long world war. That fight is still named for this port town.
A vast sea wave hit this town in the great ocean quake of 2004. The town lost more than five hundred lives in that flood.
A famed mangrove forest spreads in its district, a green maze of trees and still water. That wild wood is the mark most folk know here.
